clinician.trajectory_summary: A 28-year-old male presented with a 2-month history of nonproductive progressive cough and left flank pain, along with abdominal distention and a large mass in the left upper quadrant. Initial CT chest partially visualized a heterogeneously enhancing mass in the left retroperitoneum. Subsequent abdominal MRI revealed a large (155 × 140 × 150 mm) mass in the left suprarenal fossa with metastatic lymph nodes, and multiple metastatic nodules in the lower lobes of both lungs and liver. A total body bone scan showed no bone metastasis. Biopsy of the mass revealed small round cells on microscopic examination. Immunohistochemistry showed tumor cells positive for CK, FLI-1, and Synaptophysin, and negative for CD99, among others. The pathology report concluded that the findings were compatible with renal PNET/Ewing sarcoma.

Metastatic lymph nodes at the left side of the abdominal aorta and multiple metastatic nodules in the lower lobes of both lungs and liver were also noted, highly suggestive of neoplastic pathology.
A total body bone scan performed for staging revealed no bone metastasis.

Immunohistochemistry (IHC) on tumor cells was negative for LCA, WT-1, DESMIN, Myogenin, phox-B2, CD99, SOX10, Chromogranin, and GATA3 and positive for CK, FLI-1, and Synaptophysin.
The pathology report was compatible with renal PNET/Ewing sarcoma.
